title: Interactive 3D visualization of surface roughness predictions in additive manufacturing: A data-driven framework
summary: Builds a Box-Behnken experimental dataset relating extrusion printing parameters and local surface inclination to measured roughness, trains a multilayer perceptron on it, and deploys the predictor behind a web interface that colours an uploaded mesh face by face; a conditional GAN augments the sparsely sampled regions of the design, with the gain holding only at moderate augmentation ratios. CTGAN is cited as the tabular conditional-GAN prior art the augmenter follows, for conditioning on process descriptors to preserve feature dependencies rather than sampling unconditionally, but it is not run.
evidence: the related-work section states that for tabular data, conditional GAN variants have been developed to better capture mixed discrete and continuous variables and complex distributions, citing [13], which is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni (2019); section 3.3 describes the augmenter as a CGAN whose conditioning vector holds the scaled process parameters and the surface-inclination descriptor while the generator emits a roughness value, and states the approach is consistent with tabular CGAN methodologies developed for mixed and multimodal numerical data where conditional generation preserves feature dependencies rather than generating unconditional samples, citing [13] again. The generator is the authors' own; no CTGAN row appears in any results table

title: Generative Synthetic Data for Causal Inference: Pitfalls, Remedies, and Opportunities
summary: Shows that a synthetic table can preserve train-on-synthetic-test-on-real accuracy and privacy distance while distorting the average treatment effect, so the usual acceptance criteria do not certify a dataset for causal work, and proposes a hybrid construction that generates covariates but keeps the treatment and outcome mechanisms explicit, evaluated on simulations and an ACTG clinical trial. CTGAN is one of the two generator families the argument rests on, appearing as CTGAN Full and CTGAN Hybrid among the four synthetic ACTG datasets and named in the abstract as the comparison the language-model generator is often more faithful than.
evidence: the related-work section credits CTGAN [Xu et al., 2019] with introducing conditional GANs with mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling for tabular data; the ACTG application constructs four synthetic datasets, LLM Full, LLM Hybrid, CTGAN Full and CTGAN Hybrid, and Table 3 reports for each the train-on-synthetic-test-on-real RMSE for the cd420 outcome, the mean distance to closest record, and IPW, AIPW and TMLE treatment-effect estimates over repeated subsamples of 1000, with CTGAN's RMSE falling from 244.46 to 107.95 under hybridization; the abstract states that language-model hybrid synthesis is often more faithful than CTGAN where causal fidelity can be assessed

title: AdaPCLA: Adaptive Prior-Calibrated Logit Adjustment for Long-Tailed Longitudinal EHR Generation
summary: Addresses the tendency of autoregressive electronic health record generators to under-represent rare diagnoses by annealing a prior-calibrated adjustment into the training logits, so that tail co-occurrence structure is preserved without an external bias term at inference, and reports better tail plausibility, downstream utility and zero-shot cross-population adaptation than sequential EHR baselines. CTGAN is cited once, grouped with medGAN as the GAN and VAE prior art that improved privacy-preserving generation but did not preserve longitudinal dependency structure.
evidence: the introduction states that GAN and VAE-based methods [9, 10] improved privacy-preserving generation but often struggled to preserve longitudinal dependency structure, and the related-work section places [9, 10, 16] as the GAN, VAE and correlation-aware models for discrete or tabular medical records that longitudinal generation progressed from; reference [10] is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni (2019) and [9] is Choi et al. (2017). CTGAN is never named in the body and the compared baselines are LSTM, EVA, SynTEG, a GPT-style model and HALO, so the citation is a grouped one in a sequence-generation paper
